title: Omni-Modal LLMs Know More Than They Say
abstract: arXiv:2610.16135v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) extend LLMs to process heterogeneous modalities (e.g., vision, audio, and IMU signals) alongside language, enabling a broader range of multimodal tasks. Yet we find that these models often fail to express information from non-textual modalities even when they perceive it correctly. We term this disconnect knows-but-cannot-say. To investigate this phenomenon, we introduce Token-level Modality Alignment (TMA), which measures the alignment between individual modality representations and response representations. Our analysis shows that non-textual representations are less aligned with response tokens and receive less attention than textual representations, suggesting a potential explanation for uneven modality preferences. translated_title: 全模态大语言模型知道的比它们说出来的更多
translated_abstract: 全模态大语言模型将大语言模型扩展到能够处理异构模态（如视觉、音频和IMU信号）以及语言，从而支持更广泛的多模态任务。然而我们发现，这些模型即使正确感知了来自非文本模态的信息，也往往无法将其表达出来。我们将这种脱节现象称为“知而不能言”。为了研究这一现象，我们提出了Token级模态对齐，用于衡量单个模态表示与响应表示之间的对齐程度。我们的分析表明，非文本表示与响应token的对齐程度较低，且获得的注意力少于文本表示，这为模态偏好不均衡现象提供了一种潜在的解释。基于这些发现，我们提出了OmniCatalyst，这是一种简单的“感知→推断”策略，通过自生成的文本对原始模态输入进行补充，从而缓解这一问题……
tldr: 该论文揭示了全模态大语言模型的“知而不能言”现象——模型虽能正确感知非文本模态信息却无法表达，提出Token级模态对齐度量揭示其成因在于非文本表示对齐度低且获得的注意力少，并设计了OmniCatalyst“感知→推断”策略，利用自生成文本补充模态输入来缓解该问题。
en_tdlr: This paper uncovers the "knows-but-cannot-say" phenomenon in omni-modal LLMs, introduces Token-level Modality Alignment (TMA) to diagnose it—showing non-textual representations are less aligned and less attended—and proposes OmniCatalyst, a perceive→infer strategy that mitigates it by complementing modality inputs with self-generated text.
